title: Acetabular osteophyte-like ossification in DDH: association with labral morphology and age

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Acetabular osteophyte-like ossification in DDH: association with labral morphology and age》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · S0001-p2】During the development of the acetabulum in children, ossification primarily occurs through endochondral ossification [10]. Previous studies have shown that ossification of the acetabulum is impaired in patients with DDH, leading to a shallower and more oblique acetabulum on the affected side [11]. Conventional radiographic indices of impaired ossification include the acetabular index [12], center edge angle [13], and the acetabular depth width ratio [14]. However, abnormal ossification in DDH is not limited to under-development. The growth and development of the bony acetabulum in children is governed by the epiphyseal cartilage [15]. Osteogenesis of the epiphyseal cartilage drives expansion of the acetabular cavity, which utilizes the spherical shape of the femoral head as a growth template [11]. We observed that as LACC deformity progresses, acetabular cartilage loses support from the spherical femoral head template, preventing outward extension. Instead, the acetabular cartilage is compressed by the femoral head, bending inward and downward, and undergo premature osteophyte-like abnormal ossification. Previous animal experiments suggested that this might be related to cartilage degeneration associated with LACC inversion [16,17]. However, there is currently no clinical study on the correlation between LACC morphology and AOO. AOO alters the smooth and curved morphology of the acetabulum, compromising its congruence with the femoral head (Figure 1), with potential implications for acetabular remodeling and long-term prognosis. From a treatment perspective, such morphological alterations might affect decisions regarding closed versus open reduction by creating a bony obstacle to concentric reduction, and may also influence labral management strategies – for example, whether isolated labral incision suffices or concurrent management of the ossific protrusion is required. However, large-scale longitudinal studies are lacking, and its long-term clinical impact remains unconfirmed. Previous evidence linking LACC morphology to such ossification is limited to animal experiments [16,17], clinical data in humans are absent. In this study, we aim to investigate the imaging correlates of AOO as a foundational step toward defining its clinical relevance in preoperative planning.

【Introduction · S0001-p3】This study aims to find the correlation between LACC morphology and AOO and to assess the influence of age on the abnormal ossification by reviewing preoperative hip MRI and CT images of patients with DDH. Crucially, we sought to determine whether the role of LACC morphology is age-dependent – that is, whether its predictive value for AOO emerges specifically in older children, independent of DDH severity.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Acetabular osteophyte-like ossification in DDH: association with labral morphology and age》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Patients · S0002-S2001-p1】We retrospectively collected preoperative anteroposterior pelvic radiographs, hip MRI and CT images of patients diagnosed with DDH at our hospital between January 2015 and December 2022. The inclusion criteria were 1) patients diagnosed with DDH based on plain radiographs or CT and 2) no prior treatment before these imaging examinations. The exclusion criteria were 1) absence of coronal MRI images or poor image quality precluding assessment of LACC morphology; 2) CT reconstruction slice thickness >1 mm precluding three-dimensional analysis; 3) interval between CT and MRI examinations exceeding one month and 4) absence of standard preoperative anteroposterior pelvic radiographs or poor radiographic quality precluding radiographic assessment. All radiographic, MRI, and CT examinations were obtained as part of the preoperative evaluation, no treatment was performed during the interval between these imaging examinations. After applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria, a total of 180 patients (199 affected hips) were ultimately included (Figure 2). This study was approved by our hospital’s ethics committee (No. 2025-389) which covers retrospective analysis of imaging data from the full study period of January 2015 to December 2022. The requirement for informed consent was waived by the ethics committee due to the retrospective nature of the study, which involved the analysis of anonymized imaging data. All procedures performed in studies involving human participants were in accordance with the ethical standards of the institutional research committee and with the 1964 Helsinki Declaration and its later amendments. Data analysis for this study began on October 1, 2025.

【Patients and methods · abstract-3-1】We retrospectively reviewed preoperative pelvic radiographs, MRI, and CT images of 180 patients (199 hips) with DDH from January 2015 to December 2022. Acetabular index (AI) and Tönnis grade were assessed on radiographs, LACC morphology classified on MRI, and AOO identified on multiplanar CT reconstructions. Group comparisons, multivariable logistic regression, interaction analysis, and ROC analysis were performed.

We retrospectively reviewed preoperative pelvic radiographs, MRI, and CT images of 180 patients (199 hips) with DDH from January 2015 to December 2022. Acetabular index (AI) and Tönnis grade were assessed on radiographs, LACC morphology classified on MRI, and AOO identified on multiplanar CT reconstructions. Group comparisons, multivariable logistic regression, interaction analysis, and ROC analysis were performed.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Acetabular osteophyte-like ossification in DDH: association with labral morphology and age》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-4-1】AOO occurred in 44/146 (30.1%) inverted and 10/53 (18.9%) everted hips. In children >2 years, AOO was more frequent in the inverted group (p = 0.031), whereas no difference was found in those ≤2 years (p = 0.515). Multivariable analysis showed age was the most consistent independent correlate of AOO in the overall cohort (OR=1.022, p < 0.001). LACC morphology was not significant in the full model but became significant after excluding AI (OR=3.792, p = 0.012). In children >2 years, inverted LACC was independently associated with AOO (OR=7.66, p = 0.008), with a significant age-by-LACC interaction (p = 0.042). Age predicted AOO in both LACC groups (AUC 0.800 and 0.735). AOO predominantly involved the posterior acetabulum.

【Conclusion · abstract-5-1】Age was the most consistent independent correlate of AOO, while the effect of LACC morphology was age-dependent. Inverted LACC was strongly associated with AOO in children >2 years with a posterior predilection. These exploratory and hypothesis-generating findings require prospective validation.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Acetabular osteophyte-like ossification in DDH: association with labral morphology and age》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1. · F0001】Figure 1. A representative case of unilateral DDH with acetabular osteophyte-like ossification (AOO). a) Preoperative coronal CT shows AOO (arrow) in the right acetabulum. b) Preoperative sagittal CT demonstrates that the AOO is located in the posterior aspect of the right acetabulum(arrow). c) Coronal CT 8 months after open reduction surgery reveals AOO (arrow) in the right acetabulum as well. d) Postoperative sagittal CT shows AOO in the posterior acetabulum(arrow), with increased density and an irregular border of the femoral head. AOO alters the smooth, curved morphology of the acetabulum and results in femoral head anteversion, affecting the congruence between the acetabulum and the femoral head, leading to poor prognosis.

【Figure 2. · F0002】Figure 2. Flowchart of the enrolled patients.

【Figure 3. · F0003】Figure 3. MRI morphological classification of the labrum-acetabular cartilage complex (LACC) in DDH (arrow). a) Everted LACC. b) Inverted LACC. c) Partly inverted LACC.
